title: Kingdom of Iberia founded
description: According to the Georgian chronicles Pharnavaz I becomes the first king of Kartli, with his capital at Mtskheta.

title: Pompey invades Iberia
description: The Roman general defeats King Artoces and makes Iberia and Colchis dependants of Rome.

title: Iberia adopts Christianity
description: King Mirian III is converted by Saint Nino and makes Christianity the religion of the kingdom.

title: Tbilisi founded
description: King Vakhtang Gorgasali builds a town by the hot springs on the Kura, which his son makes the capital.

title: Bolnisi inscriptions
description: The church of Bolnisi is completed with inscriptions that are among the oldest dated examples of Georgian writing.

title: Heraclius and the Khazars besiege Tbilisi
description: The Byzantine emperor and his Turkic allies attack the Persian-held city, which the Khazars sack the following year.

title: Emirate of Tbilisi
description: After the campaign of Marwan ibn Muhammad an Arab emir is installed in Tbilisi, which stays under Muslim rule for nearly four centuries.

title: Bagrat III unites Georgia
description: Already king of Abkhazia, Bagrat inherits Kartli and becomes the first king of a united Georgia.

title: Battle of Didgori
description: King David IV defeats a much larger Seljuk coalition, opening the way to the capture of Tbilisi and the Georgian golden age.

title: David IV takes Tbilisi
description: The king captures the city from its Muslim rulers and makes it his capital.

title: Tamar becomes sole ruler
description: On the death of her father George III, Tamar is crowned a second time and begins a reign in which medieval Georgia reaches its greatest extent.

title: Jalal al-Din sacks Tbilisi
description: The Khwarazmian ruler takes and sacks the capital, a blow followed a decade later by the Mongol conquest.

title: Timur sacks Tbilisi
description: Timur captures the city and King Bagrat V in the first of eight invasions that ruin the kingdom.

title: Kingdom of Georgia divided
description: A royal council accepts the division of the country into the kingdoms of Kartli, Kakheti and Imereti and the principality of Samtskhe.

title: Battle of Marabda
description: A Safavid army defeats the Georgian rising led by Giorgi Saakadze, though resistance keeps Shah Abbas from carrying out the removal of the population of eastern Georgia.

title: First printing press in Tbilisi
description: Vakhtang VI sets up the first press in Georgia, which prints the Gospels and later the national epic.

title: Treaty of Georgievsk
description: King Heraclius II places eastern Georgia under the protection of the Russian Empire.

title: Battle of Krtsanisi
description: The Persian ruler Agha Mohammad Khan defeats Heraclius II and burns Tbilisi, while the promised Russian help does not come.

title: Russia annexes eastern Georgia
description: Tsar Alexander I abolishes the kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti and the Bagrationi monarchy, the start of more than a century of Russian rule.

title: Birth of Stalin
description: Ioseb Jughashvili, later ruler of the Soviet Union as Joseph Stalin, is born to a cobbler's family.

title: Democratic Republic of Georgia declared
description: The Georgian National Council declares independence on the collapse of the Transcaucasian federation, and a Social Democratic government holds office for three years.

title: Red Army takes Tbilisi
description: Soviet Russian troops capture the capital after ten days of fighting and Georgia becomes a Soviet republic.

title: August Uprising
description: A rising against Soviet rule is put down within weeks and followed by the execution of thousands.

title: Tbilisi demonstrations suppressed
description: Troops fire on crowds protesting against Khrushchev's criticism of Stalin, killing dozens.

title: Tbilisi tragedy
description: Soviet troops break up a peaceful rally for independence and twenty-one people die, which turns opinion firmly against Soviet rule.

title: Independence restored
description: After a referendum the Supreme Council under Zviad Gamsakhurdia declares the restoration of the independence lost in 1921.

title: Gamsakhurdia overthrown
description: The president flees after two weeks of fighting in the centre of Tbilisi, and Eduard Shevardnadze returns to lead the country in March.

title: Fall of Sukhumi
description: Abkhaz forces and their allies take the city from Georgian government troops, ending the war of 1992 to 1993 and leading to the flight of most of the Georgian population of Abkhazia.

title: Rose Revolution
description: President Eduard Shevardnadze resigns after three weeks of peaceful protests over a disputed election, and Mikheil Saakashvili is elected in his place.

title: Russo-Georgian War
description: Fighting between Georgian and South Ossetian forces becomes a five-day war with Russia, which then recognises South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent states.
